Two stages of a tadpole in side view. Left: a young tadpole with three pairs of feathery external gills (bright red) sticking out on each side behind the head. Right: an older tadpole with the gills covered by skin, and a small opening (the spiracle) on the left side, with arrows showing water entering the mouth and leaving through the spiracle. Draw only the outside of the tadpoles, as solid opaque bodies. Do not show any internal organs, no cutaway, no see-through body.
